name: The longest run of rises
brief:
`closes` holds daily closing prices in date order. A rise is a close strictly above the close before it. Write `longest_rise(closes)`, which returns the largest number of rises in a row. A flat day or a fall ends a run.

For `{100, 101, 103, 102, 104, 105, 106}` the first run has two rises, the fall to 102 ends it, and 104, 105 and 106 make three more. The answer is 3.
constraints: $0 \le n \le 10^5$ closes. With fewer than two closes there is no rise.
hint: Keep the length of the current run and the best so far. Update the best every time the run grows, not only when it ends.

examples.note: 104, 105, 106 are three rises in a row.
A flat close is not a rise.

how: Submit runs 12 hidden tests. Each answer must equal the expected value.
notes: A run counts rises, the gaps between closes, so three rising closes after a fall make three, not four.
Updating `best` inside the loop covers a run that lasts to the last close.
Starting at `i = 1` reads `closes[i - 1]` safely, and an empty vector skips the loop.

planted.slip: Counts the closes in the run, not the rises, so every answer is one too high.
Updates the best only when a run ends, so a run to the last close is lost.
Counts a flat close as a rise.
